title: Magnetic Bead Ingestion Incident: Case 2023-042
premise: A toddler ingested a detached, colorful magnetic bead from a premium stacking toy, prompting the manufacturer to issue a voluntary recall for the specific production batch.

side_A.role: an advocate at a consumer-safety group
side_A.goal: pushing for a recall of the product

side_B.goal: showing the product is safe when used as directed

documents:
=== DOCUMENT 1: Incident Log - Vance Residence, Oakhaven ===

**Date:** October 12, 2023
**Time:** 14:30
**Location:** Vance Family Residence, Oakhaven
**Weather:** Clear, 18°C (Indoor incident)

**Subject:** Ingestion of foreign object by Leo Vance (Age 2)

**Narrative Entry:**
At 14:30, parents of Leo Vance reported the child had a detached component in his mouth. The component was identified as a bright blue magnetic bead, 15mm in diameter, from the toy model 'StackPro 2000'. The bead was removed manually by the father prior to emergency transport.

**Item Identification:**
*   **Toy Model:** StackPro 2000
*   **Serial Number:** Located on base; matches Batch #492-B code.
*   **Batch Details:** #492-B, produced August 5, 2023, at Northbridge facility.
*   **Purchase Date:** July 20, 2023, from major retail chain, city center.
*   **Packaging:** Warning label present: "Choking Hazard: Small Parts. Not for children under 3 years."

**Observations:**
The bead was found to be 15mm in diameter. This dimension is below the small parts cylinder threshold of 31.7mm for children under 3. The toy utilizes a snap-fit mechanism requiring 15 Newtons of force to separate, which is a standard accepted in the industry. The specific color of the bead, bright blue, was noted by pediatric development specialists to be highly attractive to toddlers.

**Action Taken:**
Child taken to St. Mary's Hospital at 15:00 for standard observation.

=== DOCUMENT 2: Medical Report - St. Mary's Hospital ===

**Patient:** Leo Vance
**DOB:** [Redacted] (Age 2)
**Date of Visit:** October 12, 2023
**Time of Arrival:** 15:00
**Attending Physician:** Dr. A. Smith

**Chief Complaint:**
Ingestion of foreign object (magnetic bead).

**History of Present Illness:**
Patient presented with a 15mm magnetic bead in the oral cavity. The bead was removed by parental intervention prior to arrival. Patient reports no pain at time of examination.

**Physical Examination:**
*   **Oral Cavity:** No residual foreign body.
*   **Lip:** Minor abrasion on the lower lip, measuring 3mm in length.
*   **General:** Patient is alert, oriented, and asymptomatic.

**Assessment:**
Ingestion event with minor traumatic abrasion. No evidence of airway compromise or internal injury.

**Plan:**
Standard observation protocol initiated. Patient monitored for 2 hours.

**Discharge Summary:**
Patient remained asymptomatic throughout the 2-hour monitoring period. No complications observed. Discharged home with instructions to monitor for delayed symptoms. Injury described as minor and self-limiting.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Email Correspondence - PlayWell Industries ===

**From:** Marcus Thorne, Head of Communications, PlayWell Industries
**To:** Leo Vance, Sarah Vance
**Date:** October 14, 2023
**Subject:** Voluntary Recall Notice - Batch #492-B

Dear Mr. and Mrs. Vance,

We are writing to inform you of a voluntary recall notice issued today, October 14, 2023, targeting only Batch #492-B of the StackPro 2000 toy. Our records indicate that your unit, purchased on July 20, 2023, falls within this specific batch produced on August 5, 2023, at the Northbridge facility.

We understand the distress this incident has caused. Please be assured that the recall notice was distributed via email to registered users within 48 hours of the incident report. We take all safety concerns seriously.

Our internal records show that 99.8% of units in Batch #492-B passed internal quality control tests for magnet retention prior to shipment. The toy’s design uses a snap-fit mechanism that requires 15 Newtons of force to separate, a standard accepted in the industry.

As a gesture of goodwill, PlayWell Industries has arranged to provide a free replacement toy to your family. This replacement will be delivered on October 15, 2023.

We stand by the safety of our product and the adequacy of our warning labels, which state "Choking Hazard: Small Parts. Not for children under 3 years."

Sincerely,

Marcus Thorne
Head of Communications
PlayWell Industries

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statement - SafePlay Advocates ===

**Witness:** Dr. Elena Ross
**Role:** Lead Engineer, SafePlay Advocates
**Date:** October 15, 2023

I am filing this statement in response to the ingestion incident involving Leo Vance. The facts are clear and damning.

The bead detached due to a manufacturing defect in the snap-fit mechanism, which was weaker than industry standards. PlayWell Industries claims the child applied excessive force, but this is a deflection. A 2-year-old does not generate the force required to break a mechanism designed to 15 Newtons unless the mechanism itself is flawed. We have seen this before; it is a systemic design flaw.

Furthermore, the recall was issued too late, as the manufacturer knew about potential defects in Batch #492-B before the incident. They sat on this data while children were at risk. The fact that they distributed the recall via email within 48 hours does not excuse the delay in the initial announcement.

The injury was severe, as the child experienced significant distress and required immediate medical intervention. To call this "minor" is to ignore the trauma inflicted on the family. The bright blue color of the bead, highly attractive to toddlers, makes this an even greater hazard.

We filed a formal complaint with the regulatory body on October 15, 2023. We will not rest until PlayWell Industries is held accountable for this failure.

**Witness:** Sarah Jenkins
**Role:** Consumer Safety Officer, SafePlay Advocates
**Date:** October 15, 2023

I am adding my perspective on the warning labels and the severity of the incident.

The warning label was insufficiently prominent and did not adequately convey the specific risk of magnetic bead ingestion. A generic "Choking Hazard" label is not enough when the product contains high-attraction magnetic components. The label was buried in the packaging, not prominently displayed on the front where parents would see it.

The injury was severe, as the child experienced significant distress and required immediate medical intervention. The abrasion on the lip, while small in measurement, is a testament to the force involved and the danger posed. The child was not just "asymptomatic"; he was in distress until the bead was removed.

We published a press release on October 16, 2023, highlighting the incident as a systemic design flaw. This is not an isolated case; it is a pattern of negligence.

=== DOCUMENT 5: Regulatory Body Acknowledgment ===

**To:** SafePlay Advocates
**From:** Office of Consumer Safety, Regulatory Body
**Date:** October 17, 2023
**Re:** Formal Complaint - Case 2023-042

Dear Dr. Ross and Ms. Jenkins,

We acknowledge receipt of your formal complaint filed on October 15, 2023, regarding the ingestion incident involving Leo Vance and the PlayWell Industries StackPro 2000 toy (Batch #492-B).

We have reviewed the initial documentation, including the incident log from the Vance residence, the medical report from St. Mary's Hospital, and the voluntary recall notice issued by PlayWell Industries on October 14, 2023.

We note that PlayWell Industries reported that 99.8% of units in Batch #492-B passed internal quality control tests for magnet retention prior to shipment. We also note that no other injuries or reports of detached beads were recorded for Batch #492-B in the 30 days following the recall.

However, we take the concerns raised by SafePlay Advocates seriously. A review of the case has been scheduled for November 1, 2023. This review will assess the cause of the bead detachment, the adequacy of the warning labels, and the timeliness of the recall.

Please be advised that this acknowledgment does not constitute a final determination on the merits of the complaint. We will maintain neutrality in our review.

Sincerely,

Office of Consumer Safety
Regulatory Body
